name: The Gologorica–Gračišće line
route: Gologorica and Gračišće → Poreč, Crikvenica → United States, South Africa, Australia
note: David's line, and the one Carlo and Camillo belong to. It is also the line whose emigrant spelling became Defranceski — a form now concentrated in South Africa.

name: The Carnia line
note: No longer a guess about weavers in general. A De Franceschi of Mione is named on the 1679 headmen's list as working in the Habsburg County of Pazin — the same county the family's Istrian villages sit in. The route is documented; the descent is not.

name: The Pazin-county line
note: Treated as unrelated to the Carnia line by the existing research. That is an inference from an absent record, and it is challengeable.

name: The Domenico line
note: Municipal councillors by 1655, then lawyers and officials. Sparse.

name: The Ližnjan line
note: From the existing family research; no register work done yet.

name: The Dalmatian line — Omiš and Imotski
note: Almost certainly not your family. A noble house that reached Dalmatia in the fourteenth century, held a warship at Omiš by 1590, and won the Perinuša estate for storming Imotski in 1717. Their prefix was removed by decree of the Napoleonic administration, so they are Franceschi today — about 60 in Croatia, 25 of them in Split, and the only one of the three Croatian clusters that is growing.

name: The Vodnjan cluster
note: Found in the 1945 cadastre during this research and accounted for by no existing line. The largest concentration in Istria and the newest open question.

name: The Seget line — Umag
route: Crete (Candia) → Istria after 1669 → Umag and Seget → Brtonigla, Koper
note: A noble house that fled Crete when the Ottomans took it in 1669, bought the Seget estate from the Venier in 1720 and were made citizens of Umag in 1730. Marc'Antonio (1671–1758) was a physician married to a Greek wife, Crissulla Marulli; his son Alvise served as dragoman at the Ottoman Porte. Published scholarship treats them and the Gologorica family as the two Istrian branches of one family — which, if it holds, is the largest single claim anyone has made about this surname in Istria.
